steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on a video diffusion noise prior for finetuning pretrained text-to-image diffusion models into text-to-video models. Cover the motivation from text-to-image success, the cost of training video models from scratch, why i.i.d. noise is a poor choice, our model, and a list of contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Success of text-to-image diffusion; can we repeat it for video?
- Existing video diffusion models trained from scratch, and their cost
- Our approach: start from a pretrained image model; a better noise prior
- Our large-scale text-to-video model
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Text-to-image success
  - large-scale diffusion text-to-image models: complex text -> photorealistic images
  - novel concepts unseen during training
  - image editing/processing via guidance control and embedding techniques
  - success in several applications -> established image synthesis tools for content generation
  - image synthesis democratized -> ask: same success for video with large-scale text-to-video diffusion?
- Prior video diffusion models
  - Ho et al.: UNet-based architecture, joint image-video denoising losses
  - Imagen video: extends cascaded text-to-image architecture of Imagen
  - both train from scratch
  - high-quality videos, but expensive: hundreds of high-end GPUs or TPUs, several weeks of training
  - video harder: individual images + coherent temporal dynamics
  - frame formation shared with image synthesis, yet pretrained text-to-image models ignored
- Our approach
  - start from pretrained text-to-image diffusion model; reuse components -> knowledge transfer, efficient training
  - similar idea in several recent works
  - they all extend i.i.d. image noise prior to video by adding a dimension to the 2D noise map
  - not ideal: ignores natural correlations in videos already learned by image models
  - Figure 2: t-SNE of noise maps from pretrained text-to-image model; frames of same video cluster together (high correlation)
  - i.i.d. prior does not model this -> impedes finetuning
  - our analysis -> noise prior better tailored for finetuning image model to video; captures correlations (blue dots)
- Our model
  - large-scale diffusion-based text-to-video model
  - design choices from prior work: temporal attention, joint image-video finetuning, cascaded generation architecture, ensemble of expert denoisers
  - new state-of-the-art on several benchmark datasets
  - Figure 1: high-quality zero-shot video synthesis, SOTA photorealism and temporal consistency
- Contributions
  - video diffusion noise tailored for finetuning text-to-image models for text-to-video
  - extensive experimental validation of the noise prior
  - large-scale text-to-video model from pretrained eDiff-I with our noise prior; state-of-the-art on several benchmarks

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Large text-to-image models based on diffusion have shown impressive capabilities in turning complex text descriptions into photorealistic images. They can generate images with new concepts that were not seen during training. Sophisticated image editing and processing tasks can be done easily with guidance control and embedding techniques. Because of the huge success in several applications, these models are now established as powerful image synthesis tools for generating content. Since image synthesis has been largely democratized by the success of these text-to-image models, it is natural to ask if we can repeat the same success in video synthesis with large-scale text-to-video diffusion models.

There have been multiple attempts to build large-scale video diffusion models. Ho et al. proposed a UNet-based architecture for video synthesis that is trained with joint image-video denoising losses. Imagen video extends the cascaded text-to-image generation architecture of Imagen to generate videos. Both of these works train a video generation model directly from scratch. These approaches are very successful and produce high-quality videos, but they are inherently expensive to train, since they need hundreds of high-end GPUs or TPUs and several weeks of training. Video generators need to learn to form individual images, but they also need to learn to synthesize coherent temporal dynamics, and this makes video generation a lot more challenging. Forming individual frames is shared between image and video synthesis, but these works ignore that powerful pretrained text-to-image diffusion models exist and train their video generators from scratch.

- Our approach
  - start from pretrained text-to-image diffusion model; reuse components -> knowledge transfer, efficient training
  - similar idea in several recent works; they all extend i.i.d. image noise prior to video by adding a dimension to the 2D noise map
  - not ideal: ignores natural correlations in videos already learned by image models
  - Figure 2: t-SNE of noise maps from pretrained text-to-image model; frames of same video cluster together
  - i.i.d. prior does not model this -> impedes finetuning; our noise prior captures the correlations (blue dots)
- Our model
  - design choices from prior work: temporal attention, joint image-video finetuning, cascaded generation architecture, ensemble of expert denoisers
  - new state-of-the-art on several benchmark datasets
  - Figure 1: high-quality zero-shot video synthesis, SOTA photorealism and temporal consistency
- Contributions
  - video diffusion noise tailored for finetuning text-to-image models for text-to-video
  - extensive experimental validation of the noise prior
  - large-scale text-to-video model from pretrained eDiff-I with our noise prior; state-of-the-art on several benchmarks

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Large text-to-image models based on diffusion have shown impressive capabilities in turning complex text descriptions into photorealistic images. They can generate images with new concepts that were not seen during training. Sophisticated image editing and processing tasks can be done easily with guidance control and embedding techniques. Because of the huge success in several applications, these models are now established as powerful image synthesis tools for generating content. Since image synthesis has been largely democratized by the success of these text-to-image models, it is natural to ask if we can repeat the same success in video synthesis with large-scale text-to-video diffusion models.

There have been multiple attempts to build large-scale video diffusion models. Ho et al. proposed a UNet-based architecture for video synthesis that is trained with joint image-video denoising losses. Imagen video extends the cascaded text-to-image generation architecture of Imagen to generate videos. Both of these works train a video generation model directly from scratch. These approaches are very successful and produce high-quality videos, but they are inherently expensive to train, since they need hundreds of high-end GPUs or TPUs and several weeks of training. Video generators need to learn to form individual images, but they also need to learn to synthesize coherent temporal dynamics, and this makes video generation a lot more challenging. Forming individual frames is shared between image and video synthesis, but these works ignore that powerful pretrained text-to-image diffusion models exist and train their video generators from scratch.

We try a different way to build large-scale text-to-video diffusion models, which is to start from a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model. Our motivation is that most of the components learned for image synthesis can be reused effectively for video generation, which gives knowledge transfer and efficient training. Several recent works use a similar idea. All of them, when finetuning, simply extend the image diffusion noise prior (i.i.d. noise) used in the text-to-image model to a video diffusion noise prior by adding an extra dimension to the 2D noise map. We argue this is not ideal because it does not use the natural correlations in videos that the image models have already learned. Figure 2 shows this: we visualize the t-SNE plot of the noise maps for different input frames, obtained from a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model. The noise maps for different frames from the same video (blue dots) are clustered together, so they are highly correlated. The i.i.d. noise prior does not model this correlation, and this would get in the way of finetuning. We analyzed the video diffusion noise prior carefully, and this led us to a noise prior that is better suited to finetuning an image synthesis model for video generation. As the figure shows, our proposed noise prior (blue dots) captures the correlations in the noise maps of the video frames well.

Then we build a large-scale text-to-video model based on diffusion. We use several design choices from prior works, including temporal attention, joint image-video finetuning, a cascaded generation architecture and an ensemble of expert denoisers. With these techniques and the proposed video noise prior, our model sets a new state-of-the-art for video generation and outperforms competing methods on several benchmark datasets. Figure 1 shows that our model can do high-quality zero-shot video synthesis with SOTA photorealism and temporal consistency.

Our work makes the following key contributions.

- 1. We propose a video diffusion noise that is tailored for finetuning text-to-image diffusion models for text-to-video.

- 2. We do extensive experimental validation and verify that the proposed noise prior is effective.

- 3. We build a large-scale text-to-video diffusion model by finetuning a pretrained eDiff-I model with our noise prior, and get state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Large-scale diffusion-based text-to-image models [3,4,5] have demonstrated impressive capabilities in turning complex text descriptions into photorealistic images. They can generate images with novel concepts unseen during training, and sophisticated image editing and processing tasks can easily be accomplished through guidance control and embedding techniques. Due to their immense success in several applications [6,7,8], these models are established as powerful image synthesis tools for content generation. As image synthesis has been largely democratized by these text-to-image models, it is natural to ask whether the same success can be repeated in video synthesis with large-scale diffusion-based text-to-video models.

Multiple attempts have been made to build large-scale video diffusion models. Ho et al. [9] proposed a UNet-based architecture for video synthesis that is trained using joint image-video denoising losses. Imagen video [10] extends the cascaded text-to-image generation architecture of Imagen [4] to video generation. In both works, the video generation model is trained directly from scratch. While these approaches achieve great success and produce high-quality videos, they are inherently expensive to train, requiring hundreds of high-end GPUs or TPUs and several weeks of training. After all, video generators must learn not only to form individual images but also to synthesize coherent temporal dynamics, which makes video generation much more challenging. Although forming individual frames is shared between image and video synthesis, these works disregard the existence of powerful pretrained text-to-image diffusion models and train their video generators from scratch.

We explore a different avenue for building large-scale text-to-video diffusion models: starting from a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model. Our motivation is that most components learned for image synthesis can be effectively reused for video generation, leading to knowledge transfer and efficient training. Several recent works adopt a similar idea [11,12,13]. Without exception, when finetuning, they naively extend the image diffusion noise prior (i.i.d. noise) of the text-to-image model to a video diffusion noise prior by adding an extra dimension to the 2D noise map. We argue that this is not ideal, as it does not utilize the natural correlations in videos already learned by the image models. Figure 2 illustrates this with a t-SNE plot of noise maps corresponding to different input frames, obtained from a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model. Noise maps of different frames from the same video (blue dots) are clustered together, exhibiting a high degree of correlation. An i.i.d. noise prior does not model this correlation, which would impede finetuning. Careful analysis of the video diffusion noise prior leads us to a noise prior better tailored for finetuning an image synthesis model to the video generation task. As illustrated in the figure, our proposed noise prior (blue dots) aptly captures the correlations in noise maps of video frames.

We then build a large-scale diffusion-based text-to-video model, leveraging several design choices from prior works, including temporal attention [9], joint image-video finetuning [9], a cascaded generation architecture [10], and an ensemble of expert denoisers [5]. Together with these techniques and the proposed video noise prior, our model establishes a new state-of-the-art for video generation, outperforming competing methods on several benchmark datasets. Figure 1 shows that our model achieves high-quality zero-shot video synthesis with SOTA photorealism and temporal consistency.

In short, our work makes the following key contributions.

- 1. We propose a video diffusion noise tailored for finetuning text-to-image diffusion models for text-to-video.

- 2. We conduct extensive experimental validation and verify the effectiveness of the proposed noise prior.

- 3. We build a large-scale text-to-video diffusion model by finetuning a pretrained eDiff-I model with our noise prior, achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks.
